summary: Hyoung Seok Ham is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge, was affiliated there in 2010, and serves as Professor at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōkai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.
Hōkei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor (attested 1930).

Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Lancaster, he was Professor Emeritus at the University of Cumbria (~1986–2014) and held posts at Oxford, Lancaster, and National University of Singapore.

Ian James Coghlan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki.

Ian Reader (born 1949) specializes in Japanology and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at the University of Leeds (~1979–1983), he held posts at Kobe University of Commerce, Stirling (~1989–1995), Hawaii (~1999–2000), and Lancaster (~2003–2008).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Peshawar under Muhammad Farooq Swati in 2007. He serves as Associate Professor and Department Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and later held positions at Otani University Junior College (~1972–1980) and Otani University (~1970–2004).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held posts at Kokugakuin (~1952–1960), Tohoku (~1960–1967), University of Tokyo (~1967–1971), and Seijo University (~1971–1974).
Ichiro Katayama (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University from ~1961 to 1965 and later served as a professor there from ~1985 to 2012.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a linguistics and history scholar. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1864–1869) and later held an academic post there from ~1877 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941) and worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1960–1998).

Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University. His teachers included Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa (born 1968) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held part-time lecturer posts at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who held research positions at Otani University and Kyoto University in 2017.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Helsinki (~1983–1993) under René Gothóni, later working as an Academy Research Fellow there (1984) and visiting researcher at Oxford (~1996–1997).

Imre Galambos (born 1967) specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. Educated at ELTE, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD ~2002), he worked at the British Library (~2002–2012) before becoming a lecturer at the University of Cambridge in 2012.

Imre Hamar (born 1967) is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and National Taiwan Normal University, later becoming a professor at Eötvös Loránd University (~2002, ~2008) and visiting professor at Otani University (~2009–2010).
